note: Approved-style examples. The Writer uses these as few-shot targets. Each pairs a source recipe (as ingested) with the rewrite.

source.title: Steak with Chipotle Cheese Sauce
ingredients: 1 (10.75 ounce) can Campbell's® Condensed Cheddar Cheese Soup
1 (2 pound) skirt or beef flank steak, 1-inch thick, cut into 8 pieces

rewrite.title: Grilled Skirt Steak with Smoky Chipotle Cheddar Sauce
rewrite.headnote: Skirt steak is the cut that rewards impatience. It's thin and loose-grained, and it packs more beefy flavor per bite than steaks that cost twice as much. The only rules are heat and the knife: cook it hard and fast, then slice it against the grain, or you'll be chewing until Tuesday.
ingredients: 2 pounds skirt or flank steak, cut into 8 pieces
directions: Pat the steak dry and salt it well on both sides. If you can give it 30 to 40 minutes on the counter, do: the salt draws out moisture, dissolves in it, and soaks back in as seasoning.
Heat the oil in a 2-quart saucepan over medium heat. Add the onions and cook, stirring now and then, for about 5 minutes, until soft and just starting to turn golden.
Add the butter. When it melts, sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the milk and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Turn the heat to low and stir in the cheddar a handful at a time until smooth. Stir in the chipotle and tomatoes. Keep it warm but don't let it boil, or the cheese turns grainy.
Heat the grill to high and oil the grates. Grill skirt steak 3 to 4 minutes per side (flank 5 to 6) until the center reads 130°F for medium-rare. Rest 5 minutes.
Slice thinly against the grain, spoon the sauce over, and scatter with cilantro.
tips: Why it works: a from-scratch cheese sauce takes five extra minutes and tastes like cheese instead of the can it came in. The chipotle brings smoke, the fresh tomato cuts the richness.

rewrite.title: Slow-Oven Round Steak in Onion-Mushroom Gravy
rewrite.headnote: Round steak is lean, hardworking muscle, and it will punish you for rushing it. Give it two and a half hours in a low oven, though, and it goes from shoe leather to fork-tender. The canned soups are a shortcut and they make no apologies for it: this is a dump-and-wait supper that tastes like you tried harder.
ingredients: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup
1 (10.5 ounce) can condensed French onion soup
directions: Heat the oven to 325°F. Trim any thick fat from the steak, cut it into serving pieces, and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in an ovenproof roasting pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the steak about 1 minute per side, just long enough to brown it. Brown is flavor; gray is not.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in both soups and the water, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom, and turn the steak to coat it.
Cover tightly with a lid or foil and bake for 2 1/2 hours, until a fork slides into the meat with no resistance.

rewrite.title: Skillet Philly-Style Steak Sandwiches
rewrite.headnote: Purists will tell you a real one needs a flat-top griddle, a particular roll and a loud opinion about cheese. This one needs a skillet and about twenty minutes. The trick is slicing the beef thin and searing it in batches; crowd the pan and the meat steams instead of browning.
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon each salt, black pepper, paprika, chili powder, onion powder and garlic powder
1/2 teaspoon each dried thyme, marjoram and basil
1 green bell pepper, cut into thin strips
directions: Put the sirloin in the freezer for 20 minutes; firm meat slices thin far more easily. Cut it into thin strips about 2 inches long.
Mix the salt, pepper, paprika, chili powder, onion powder, garlic powder and herbs in a small bowl. Toss with the beef.
Heat half the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Sear the beef in two batches, about 2 minutes per batch, until browned at the edges. Set aside.
Add the remaining oil and cook the onion and pepper for 5 to 6 minutes, until soft and charred in spots.
Heat the broiler. Divide the beef among the rolls, top with the vegetables and the cheese, and broil on a baking sheet for 1 to 2 minutes, until the cheese melts. Close and serve.
